messages:
Leah: heads up — eu-west3 GPU attach failures spiked ~10% over the last 30m. graph shows attach latency aligned with an nvme temp surge on scratch cohort C.
Ravi: ouch. is this the scrub wave we've seen before?
Leah: looks like a firmware-initiated scrub escalation on a subset of nodes (cohort C). drives started triggering background full-scrub heuristics when temp > 65C, which ramps IO and write amplification.
Marta: are nodes going readonly or actually failing attaches?
Leah: not readonly. mostly long iowait during attach which causes the attach coordinator to retry, so jobs queue and GPU provision delays. attach success rate still high but tail latency is killing autoscaler decisions.
Ravi: can you paste the relevant dmesg snip?
Leah: ```
[ 1123.451234] nvme0: temperature sensor reading 67C, firmware: fw-2025-07
[ 1123.451567] nvme0: scrub: escalated to full-scan due to thermal hysteresis
[ 1124.782000] nvme0: write amplification spike: WA=2.8 -> 4.6, io_wait ms=210
[ 1125.001234] attach_coordinator: attach_wait 1200ms (retries=2)```
Kai: thanks. that WA jump is nasty. could be a firmware scheduling regression that changed flush/window heuristics.
Marta: which nodes exactly? can we move new GPU requests away from cohort C?
Leah: cohort C node list: gnode-eu3-14{1..6}. I proposed a soft-evict (drain non-critical batches) and temporarily prefer eu-west1 for new capacity until scrub quiesces.
Ravi: what's the cost impact of preferring another region vs delaying scrub?
Leah: preferring eu-west1 adds inter-region latency for customers ~20-40ms and +~12% infra egress cost for internal control traffic. Delaying scrub increases write amplification risk and might accelerate wear — long-term cost unknown. short-term, shifting a small % of provisioned jobs costs less than throttled SLAs.
Kai: can janitor throttle scrub concurrency? we tuned it before.
Marta: janitor has a concurrency knob per-pool. we can reduce concurrency for cohort C to one at a time and raise backoff windows. downside: backlog grows and we might hit a health alert.
Leah: suggestion: immediate mitigation = reduce janitor.concurrency to 1 for cohort C, set janitor.max_io_bytes to 60% for that cohort, and add an attach routing policy to deprioritize gnode-eu3-14*. They can run a staggered scrub later during overnight window.
Ravi: +1. can you run the commands? also add a temporary route in the smart-router to avoid new attaches to that node set.
Leah: running now. ```
# set janitor knobs
jq '.pools["cohort-c"].concurrency=1 | .pools["cohort-c"].max_io_bytes=0.6' /etc/janitor/config.yaml > /tmp/janitor.patch && sudo mv /tmp/janitor.patch /etc/janitor/config.yaml && sudo systemctl reload janitor
# pin smart-router
redis-cli HSET router:weights "gnode-eu3-14" 0.05
```
janitor-bot: updated janitor config for cohort-c (concurrency=1, max_io_bytes=60%). rolling restart will apply within 60s.
Leah: added router weight tweak; new attaches should avoid cohort C within next minute. monitoring dashboards: attach tail latency dropping in last 30s — will watch for an hour.
Marta: please file a follow-up to investigate fw-2025-07 change logs with vendor. might need advisory or rollback if this repeats.
Ravi: agree. tag infra-owners +eng-runtime. also capture a cost estimate for a 24h cross-region shift.
Leah: filing doc now and pinging vendor. will post an incident note if we see any node hit readonly or S.M.A.R.T errors. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
Kai: thanks — nice quick mitigation. keep me posted on the vendor reply.
